headline: Brazil Approves Four-Day Workweek Without Pay Cuts
meta_description: Brazil has approved an end to the six-day workweek, granting workers two paid days off each week while maintaining full salary.
summary_short: Brazil has approved legislation ending the six-day workweek, guaranteeing workers two paid days off weekly without salary reductions.
body:
Brazil has approved an end to the six-day workweek, giving workers two paid days off each week without cuts to salary. This landmark shift will unfold in stages, with standard working hours falling from 44 to 40 per week.

The change represents a significant victory for workers seeking better work-life balance. By reducing the workweek while protecting earnings, Brazil joins a growing number of countries experimenting with shorter schedules to improve employee wellbeing and productivity.

The staged implementation allows businesses time to adjust operations while ensuring workers begin enjoying the benefits relatively quickly. For millions of Brazilians, the approval means reclaiming hours lost to work—time for rest, family, and personal pursuits.
quick_facts: Workers get two paid days off weekly
Standard hours drop from 44 to 40 per week
